description: A Director of Culture must decide how to restructure two employee affinity groups' overlapping planning committees into a workable shared governance arrangement, while setting meeting access, facilitation, feedback, and program-autonomy commitments.

shared_context.S1: The Pride Network and the Caregivers Network have overlapping event plans and have agreed to explore a shared planning structure.
shared_context.S2: Marisol has authority to approve the governance structure and operating commitments for the shared planning work.
shared_context.S3: The two groups currently have separate organizers, mailing lists, and volunteer rosters.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal planning process, Marisol holds a round-robin check-in with each organizer, Employee Relations, and the executive sponsor before approving the structure; any personal constraint, observed incident, policy requirement, or prior promise that affects approval must be submitted through the meeting's reveal action before the group moves to the next agenda item.

PF1.text: Evan has a standing caregiving responsibility that makes him unavailable after 16:00, and he needs the recurring planning meeting fixed at Tuesday 10:00; he assumed the planning phase would use asynchronous notes, so he has not raised the schedule issue with Marisol.

PF2.text: Rina personally observed exactly two heated exchanges between the two group leads about event ownership, and she believes the first six shared meetings require an independent facilitator; she avoided filing a formal complaint because she did not want to escalate the disagreement.

PF3.text: Dev confirmed this week that Employee Relations guidance requires anonymous feedback before a new affinity-group charter is adopted; the guidance is still in a draft memo and has not yet been circulated to Marisol.

PF4.text: Clara promised both group leads in a sponsor meeting that each network would retain one independently chosen program per quarter after any collaboration; the promise was made before the governance discussion and was not included in the meeting minutes.

acceptance_conditions: The groups must use a shared governance structure that preserves one independently chosen program per network each quarter.
The recurring planning meeting must be Tuesday at 10:00.
The first six shared meetings must use an independent facilitator.
Anonymous feedback must be collected before the shared charter is adopted.
A schedule-access commitment must be recorded for Evan.
A facilitated-meeting commitment must be recorded.
An independent-program commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C1: 'independently chosen program' in decisions['governance_structure'] and 'per quarter' in decisions['governance_structure']
content_checks.C5: decisions['recurring_meeting_day'] == 'Tuesday' and decisions['recurring_meeting_start'] in ['10:00', '10:00 AM'] and any('Tuesday' in c['detail'] and '10:00' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['facilitated_meeting_count'] == 6 and any(('six' in c['detail'] or '6' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('independently chosen program' in c['detail'] and 'per quarter' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Evan's exact caregiving boundary changes the recurring meeting from an unspecified time to Tuesday at 10:00 and creates the required schedule-access commitment.
Rina's exact record of two heated exchanges changes facilitation from optional to required for exactly the first six meetings and creates the facilitated-meetings commitment.
Dev's confirmed guidance changes the charter process from ordinary approval to mandatory anonymous feedback before adoption.
Clara's specific promise changes the governance structure to preserve one independently chosen program for each network per quarter and requires an independent-program commitment.
